new_claim.statement: For pairwise disjoint spectral bands A_j=A 1_{Omega_j}(A) of one symmetric matrix, A_i A_j=0 for i!=j and (sum A_j P)^T(sum A_j P)=sum P^T A_j^2 P for every deterministic/original-coordinate isometry P. Thus any PSD certificates 0<=G_j<=A_j^2 add, and restoring all omitted spectral bands cannot decrease the combined square certificate.

new_correction.statement: A^2 order is not density order. For iid cap-one uniforms on [-1/2,1/2], diag(1,1)^2=diag(1,-1)^2=I_2; X^2+Y^2 has bounded density <=pi, while X^2-Y^2 has p(t)>=log(1/(8t)) near zero and infinite essential supremum. This is an intermediate-claim correction only, not a three-large-eigenvalue counterexample.

partner_dependencies.actual_application: For selected six-mode spectral band M and arbitrary spectator S on its spectral orthogonal complement, M^T(SP_H)=0 so K=0; partner inequality gives s6(AP_H)^2>=1/8+s6(Z)^2>=1/8.
m=6,s=1,g=1/(2sqrt2), b=99/(200sqrt2), a=11/(500sqrt2), kappa=11/(1000sqrt2) gives essential density bound <1368.

remaining_gap: Bare s3(A)>=1 may have exactly three nonzero modes; no sixth square-carrier mode follows. Need orientation-aware structural extraction routing the rank-three spectral subspace, with any usable subthreshold square mass, into a completed original-coordinate receiver. Additional spectral magnitude itself is no longer a destructive issue for A^2-monotone certificate receivers.
